keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1024-1035: Cliopatria has no Chernigov shape before 1056. The page: Mstislav 'established rule over the principality of Chernigov' in 1024 and 'set the Dnieper as the boundary with his brother Yaroslav the Wise'; the rus dossier draws the east bank as the Chernigov land and Poltava. The page gives no area. Chernigov is part of Kiev's realm again from 1036 (no shape 1036-1053).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1054-1055: Yaroslav 'bequeathed the Principality of Chernigov to his second eldest surviving son, along with Murom' (Murom page), and the Kievan Rus' page gives 'Principality of Chernigov and Tmutarakan' to Sviatoslav II in 1054. Cliopatria's first shape is 1056 and lacks the Murom-Ryazan lands to 1071; they are added from Cliopatria's Ryazan row (the 264 cells that Chernigov holds from 1072). Tmutarakan is on the Black Sea; the Chernigov page gives no date for its loss ('eventually overtaken'), so it is not drawn.

correction.text: Chernigov with the Murom-Ryazan lands: 'bequeathed the Principality of Chernigov to his second eldest surviving son, along with Murom' (Murom page)

keyframe_review.note: 224,200 km2 for 1056-1071, which lacks 180 cells of the Murom-Ryazan lands that Cliopatria adds in 1072. The Murom page makes Murom part of Chernigov's inheritance from the 1054 division, so the Ryazan-row cells are added from 1056. The page gives no infobox area to compare with.

265,800 km2: the 1056 shape plus the Murom-Ryazan lands (exactly the 264 cells of Cliopatria's Principality of Ryazan shape). Right for the pages: Murom 'changed hands seven times' in 1077-1097, 'usually alternating between Sviatoslav's sons and Vladimir Monomakh', and 'was recognized as a family possession of Sviatoslav's sons'.

correction.text: Chernigov with the Murom-Ryazan lands: 'bequeathed the Principality of Chernigov to his second eldest surviving son, along with Murom' (Murom page)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria cuts the Murom-Ryazan lands off in 1094 (200,700 km2) and starts Principality of Ryazan there. The Council of Liubech page (19 October 1097) gives 'Oleg, Davyd, and Yaroslav (sons of Sviatoslav II): Chernigov, Tmutarakan, Ryazan, and Murom', and the Murom page has Murom 'a separate principality' only 'In 1127' (Ryazan separating after 1129). So the Ryazan lands stay with Chernigov for 1094-1126; new keyframe _1127 carries the shape from then. The principality-of-ryazan dossier (eu-16-c) starts in 1094 as Cliopatria does.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1127-1235: Cliopatria's 1094 shape (Chernigov without Murom-Ryazan) is right from 1127: 'In 1127, it became a separate principality' and 'The youngest, Yaroslav, ruled in Murom and Ryazan from 1127' (Murom page, infobox 'Established 1127'). The Chernigov page: the principality 'later split into three apanage principalities: Chernigov proper, Novgorod-Seversk, and Murom-Ryazan', without dates. 200,700 km2; the page gives no area.

200,700 km2 for 1236-1240, the 1094 shape. The Mongol invasion page: 'In the winter of 1239, he sacked Chernigov and Pereyaslavl'; its inhabitants fled north; the page describes no later annexation, so the land stays with the principality until Cliopatria's Mongol shape of 1241.

ledger.note: 1024: Mstislav, son of Vladimir the Great, arrives from Tmutarakan and founds the principality of Chernigov. 'Mstislav of Chernigov ... arrived from Tmutarakan and "established rule over the principality of Chernigov"'; 'He set the Dnieper as the boundary with his brother Yaroslav the Wise.' Infobox: Established 1024. The region is the east bank, the researcher's reading of the Dnieper boundary.

ledger.note: 1036: Mstislav dies and Chernigov passes to Kiev. 'Mstislav died after a hunting trip, and "Chernigov was incorporated into the realm of Kiev"'; Yaroslav then 'gained sole authority and claimed Chernigov until 1054'. The state has no land 1036-1053.

region.text: Chernigov with the Murom-Ryazan lands: 'bequeathed the Principality of Chernigov to his second eldest surviving son, along with Murom' (Murom page)

ledger.note: 1054: Yaroslav's death gives Chernigov, with Tmutarakan, to Sviatoslav II. Kievan Rus' page: 'Principality of Chernigov and Tmutarakan, for Sviatoslav II of Kiev', map 'after the death of Yaroslav I in 1054' (Yaroslav died 20 February 1054, Yaroslav the Wise page infobox). The Murom page adds that Chernigov was bequeathed 'along with Murom'; the Murom-Ryazan lands are drawn from Cliopatria's Ryazan row. Tmutarakan is not drawn.

region.text: Murom and Ryazan, the 264 cells of Cliopatria's Ryazan shape

ledger.note: 1127: Murom-Ryazan becomes a separate principality. 'In 1127, it became a separate principality'; 'The youngest, Yaroslav, ruled in Murom and Ryazan from 1127'; after Yaroslav's death in 1129 his sons received Murom and Ryazan separately. Cliopatria cuts these lands in 1094 and starts its Ryazan row then; the page's date is 1127.
1239: Batu's armies reach Chernigov. 'In the winter of 1239, he sacked Chernigov and Pereyaslavl.' The page gives no month.

1239: Chernigov falls to the Mongols and its inhabitants flee north; 'Prince Michael of Kiev ... later lost Chernigov'. The mongol-empire dossier records Chernigov as a Mongol vassal from 1239 (the page: principalities that avoided conquest were forced 'to accept Mongol supremacy in the form of tribute').

1240: Cliopatria's last Chernigov shape; from 1241 the land is inside the Mongol shape. The pages give no end for the principality: the Chernigov page runs it to 1402 as a vassal of the Golden Horde (1245-1362) and then Lithuania; the sack of 1239 is its last dated event. Confidence 1: the year is Cliopatria's.

wars.outcome: The Mongols sack Chernigov in the winter of 1239; its inhabitants flee north and the land comes under Mongol supremacy, which 'lasted into the 14th century'.
wars.note: The Kalka River (31 May 1223) is the first Mongol victory over 'several principalities'; the page extracted does not name Chernigov in it.

certainty.note: Forest, steppe and river frontiers (the Dnieper from 1024, the Oka side of the Murom lands, the Polovtsian steppe on the south-east) never fixed by treaty or survey; the Council of Liubech (19 October 1097) assigns princes to principalities without a boundary.

notes:
Start 1024, not Cliopatria's 1056: the Chernigov page gives 'Established 1024' (Mstislav) and 'incorporated into the realm of Kiev' in 1036, and the rus dossier (eu-16-a) already carries a 1024 loss and a 1036 gain with this state as counterpart. The state has no land 1036-1053 and is re-established by Yaroslav's division in 1054. Cliopatria's first shape is 1056; keyframes cover 1024-1035 and 1054-1055 as new ones.

Murom-Ryazan: the Murom page puts Murom in Chernigov's inheritance of 1054 and makes the separate principality 1127 (Ryazan after 1129), against Cliopatria's 1072 gain and 1094 cut (the Ryazan row starts 1094). This dossier follows the pages: Murom-Ryazan is Chernigov's for 1054-1126 (union with Cliopatria's Ryazan 1094 shape) and a loss to principality-of-ryazan is dated 1127. The principality-of-ryazan dossier (eu-16-c) starts Ryazan in 1094 and so draws those 264 cells twice for 1094-1126; either its start should move to 1127 or the keyframes _1054, _1056 and _1094 here should be dropped. Not resolved here.

Disagreement inside the Chernigov page: it says 'After Sviatoslav's death [1076] the Council of Liubech decided that his sons Oleg and Davyd ... would hold the principality', but the Council of Liubech page dates the council to 19 October 1097. 1097 is used.

Unsettled / not on a page opened: the Tmutarakan holding (page: 'eventually overtaken', undated; outside every Cliopatria shape); the Novgorod-Seversk apanage (named, undated); the 1146-1240 Chernigov holdings of Kiev (the Kiev page's prince list shows Vsevolod II Olgovich 1139-1146 and Mikhail Vsevolodovich 1238-1243 on the throne; no territory); the Polovtsian wars; Kalka (1223) participation; 'Starodub, Trubchevsk, Kozelsk, Novgorod-Seversky' named as cities without dates; Bryansk and Karachev after 1240. The page gives no infobox area, so Cliopatria's 224,000-266,000 km2 could not be compared.

Mongol end: Cliopatria's shape runs to 1240, the page's last event is the winter of 1239; the dissolve is confidence 1 at 1240. The mongol-empire dossier carries the vassal_start for Chernigov in 1239 and the Lithuanian takeover c. 1357 belongs to grand-duchy-of-lithuania.
